questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? Cricket, Football, Chess, Hockey
questions.explanation: C is correct. Cricket, Football and Hockey are outdoor team sports played with a ball or puck. Chess is an indoor board game requiring no physical movement.

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? Rose, Lily, Tulip, Mango
questions.explanation: D is correct. Rose, Lily and Tulip are flowers. Mango is a fruit.

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? Square, Circle, Triangle, Volume
questions.explanation: D is correct. Square, Circle and Triangle are 2D geometric shapes. Volume is a 3D measurement concept, not a shape.

questions.stem: Which number is the odd one out? 4, 9, 25, 36, 49
questions.explanation: C is correct. 4=2², 9=3², 25=5², 49=7² — squares of prime numbers. 36=6² and 6 is NOT prime. 36 is the odd one out.

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? Violin, Guitar, Flute, Sitar
questions.explanation: C is correct. Violin, Guitar and Sitar are string instruments played by plucking or bowing. Flute is a wind instrument played by blowing.

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? Diamond, Gold, Silver, Copper
questions.explanation: A is correct. Gold, Silver and Copper are metals. Diamond is a non-metal (an allotrope of carbon).

questions.stem: Which month is the odd one out? January, March, May, June
questions.explanation: D is correct. January, March and May have 31 days. June has only 30 days.

questions.stem: Which number is the odd one out? 1, 4, 9, 16, 20
questions.explanation: D is correct. 1=1², 4=2², 9=3², 16=4² — all perfect squares. 20 is not a perfect square (√20 ≈ 4.47).

questions.stem: Which gemstone is the odd one out? Amethyst, Topaz, Emerald, Pearl
questions.explanation: D is correct. Amethyst, Topaz and Emerald are minerals — inorganic crystalline gemstones. Pearl is organic, formed inside oysters and molluscs; it is not a mineral.

questions.stem: Which is the odd one out? HCl, H₂SO₄, H₂CO₃, NaOH
questions.explanation: D is correct. HCl (hydrochloric acid), H₂SO₄ (sulphuric acid) and H₂CO₃ (carbonic acid) are all acids. NaOH (sodium hydroxide) is a strong base, not an acid.
